questions.title: Sum and maximum
questions.statement: Given n integers, print their sum and the largest value, separated by a space.
questions.output_format: Two integers: sum and maximum. The sum may not fit in 32 bits.
hints: One pass over the numbers can track two things at the same time. Which two variables do you need, and what should each one start as?
Start the maximum at the FIRST number, not 0: every number may be negative. The sum can reach 10^14, so which Java type must hold it?

read n
long sum = 0
long max = (first number)
for each number v:
    sum += v
    if (____) max = v
print sum + " " + max

solutions.name: Simplest
solutions.note: Scanner is easy to write but slow on big inputs; fine up to ~10^5 numbers.

solutions.name: Ideal
solutions.note: Same loop with fast input (BufferedReader + StringTokenizer). This is what to write in an interview or contest. Key point: long for the sum, max starts from the data, not 0.

questions.title: Reverse the array
questions.statement: Given n integers, print them in reverse order.
questions.output_format: n integers on one line, separated by spaces.
hints: You do not need a new array. Either print from the last index down to the first, or swap elements in place.
Printing 100,000 numbers one System.out.print at a time is slow. Build the whole line in a StringBuilder and print once.

read the n numbers into a[]
i = 0, j = n - 1
while (i < j):
    swap a[i] and a[j]
    ____
append a[0..n-1] to a StringBuilder with spaces; print it

solutions.name: Simplest
solutions.note: Walk the array backwards while building the output.

solutions.name: Ideal (two pointers)
solutions.note: In-place swap from both ends: the pattern behind many array questions (palindromes, partitioning). Pattern name: two pointers, opposite ends.

questions.title: Palindrome check
questions.statement: Given a string of lowercase letters, print YES if it reads the same forwards and backwards, otherwise NO.
hints: A palindrome's first character matches its last, its second matches its second-last, and so on. What can you compare?
Use two indices, one at each end, moving towards each other. Stop at the first mismatch. You never need to build the reversed string.

solutions.name: Simplest
solutions.note: Reverse a copy and compare. Short and correct; uses extra memory for the copy.

solutions.name: Ideal (two pointers)
solutions.note: Compare from both ends and exit early on the first mismatch. Same pattern as q2.

questions.title: Second largest distinct value
questions.statement: Given n integers, print the second largest DISTINCT value. If all values are equal (or n = 1), print -1.
hints: Sorting works, but can you do it in one pass by remembering just two values?

Keep `first` (largest) and `second` (largest value strictly smaller than first). A new value bigger than first pushes first down into second. Values EQUAL to first must be ignored, or duplicates break it.

solutions.name: Simplest (TreeSet)
solutions.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
solutions.note: A TreeSet removes duplicates and keeps order; the answer is the element just below the largest.

solutions.name: Ideal (one pass)
solutions.note: Two running variables. The trap is duplicates of the maximum: the `v < first` check handles it.

questions.title: Move zeros to the end
questions.statement: Given n integers, move every 0 to the end while keeping the non-zero values in their original order. Print the result.
questions.output_format: n integers on one line, separated by spaces.
hints: Shifting the whole array left every time you see a zero is correct but costs O(n) per zero: too slow for 200,000 numbers. Think about where the NEXT non-zero value should go.
Keep a write index k. Copy each non-zero value to a[k] and move k forward. After the loop, everything from k to the end becomes 0. Order is kept automatically.

solutions.name: Simplest (shifting)
solutions.note: Correct, but each zero shifts the rest of the array. It passes small tests and TIMES OUT on the large hidden test: a good example of correct-but-too-slow.
solutions.verified: 6/7 tests (times out on the large test)

solutions.name: Ideal (write index)
solutions.note: One pass with a write pointer, then fill zeros. Pattern name: two pointers, same direction (read/write).

solutions.name: Most optimized (swap, single pass)
solutions.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space, one pass
solutions.note: Moves each non-zero into position k and zeroes the old slot, so no second fill loop. Same complexity as the ideal one, so either is a full-marks interview answer.
